items.stem: What is the primary benefit of rendering a component inside a shadow DOM?

options.text: Its internal markup and styles are encapsulated from the surrounding page
options.rationale: Correct: the shadow tree scopes styles and structure so the page and component do not interfere.

options.text: It makes the component load faster than any alternative
options.rationale: Encapsulation is about isolation, not a guaranteed speed gain.

options.text: It removes the need to define a custom element
options.rationale: A custom element is still defined; shadow DOM is its internal tree.

options.text: It lets page CSS freely restyle the component internals
options.rationale: Shadow DOM prevents, not enables, arbitrary external styling of internals.

items.explanation: Correct: the shadow tree scopes styles and structure so the page and component do not interfere.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about a custom element's lifecycle are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: connectedCallback runs when the element is inserted into the document
options.rationale: Correct: connectedCallback fires on insertion and is a safe place for setup.

options.text: attributeChangedCallback runs for attributes listed in observedAttributes
options.rationale: Correct: only observed attributes trigger the callback.

options.text: The constructor is the right place to inspect child elements and attributes
options.rationale: Children and attributes may not be ready in the constructor; defer that work to connectedCallback.

options.text: Lifecycle callbacks only work inside a specific framework
options.rationale: They are part of the standard and work framework-independently.

items.explanation: Correct: connectedCallback fires on insertion and is a safe place for setup.

items.stem: A parent needs to know when a custom rating element's value changes. What is the idiomatic mechanism?

options.text: Dispatch a custom event from the element that the parent listens for
options.rationale: Correct: custom events are the standard way a web component notifies listeners of changes.

options.text: Have the parent poll the element's internals every second
options.rationale: Polling is wasteful and brittle compared with an event.

options.text: Reach into the element's shadow DOM from the parent
options.rationale: Reaching into internals breaks encapsulation and the component contract.

options.text: Reload the page on every change
options.rationale: Reloading destroys state and is not a notification mechanism.

items.explanation: Correct: custom events are the standard way a web component notifies listeners of changes.
